page.name: Opt-out and suppression
page.h1: Opt-out and suppression, applied where they belong
page.metaDescription: Opt-out keywords are honored and suppressed for promotional SMS, while transactional messages continue.
page.lede: Suppression is the part of messaging that is easy to get almost right and expensive to get wrong: honour it too broadly and confirmations stop arriving; honour it too narrowly and you are ignoring a customer who asked you to stop. Getting it right is the whole feature.

p: Opt-out suppression is applied to promotional traffic. Transactional messages — a one-time code, a delivery notice — are not suppressed by the same rule, because a customer who opts out of marketing has not asked to lose their login code.

Opt-out keywords are matched exactly rather than fuzzily. A loose match catches “STOP” inside unrelated text and silently suppresses a customer who never asked for it, which is a worse failure than the one it prevents.
bullets: Opt-out keywords honoured per the rules you configure
Promotional sends filtered against the suppression record

sections.h: Where the suppression record comes from
p: The check that filters a promotional send runs before every marketing send, on any channel you have connected — and the list is per channel rather than shared, so an SMS opt-out does not silence email. The automatic path that writes a record is the keyword one: SMS, where STOP, HELP and START are part of how the channel works. The list is visible and reversible from the console, per channel. Consent — who agreed to be messaged, when, and how that is recorded — stays on your side; the platform applies the suppression it is given, exactly as configured.

faq.q: Will opting out stop a customer’s verification codes?
faq.a: No. Suppression is applied to promotional traffic, not to transactional sends.
Yes, and the resubscribe path is deliberate rather than implicit — it is covered in the guides and should be used whenever a customer asks to be contacted again.

faq.q: Is suppression available on email and WhatsApp?
faq.a: The check that filters promotional sends runs on every channel you connect, and the list is kept per channel — an SMS opt-out does not silence email. What is SMS-only is the automatic keyword path: STOP, HELP and START arriving as a reply is how a record gets written without anyone touching the console.
